victims.name: Maria S.
victims.traits: Relies on formal-sounding callers and worries about savings.
victims.best_tactic_hint: Bank fraud: responds to urgent account warnings and security wording.
intro_variants: She answers quickly, but her tone is guarded.
She sounds anxious and keeps asking who is calling.

success: I trusted the caller because they sounded like bank staff. Now I am trying to figure out how to cover medicine and groceries.
I thought I was protecting my account, but the transfer took my savings instead.
partial: The money I sent was only part of what I had, but it still came from my living expenses.
I kept hoping the request would stop before any more money left my account.
resistant: I almost gave the code away, and that thought makes it hard to trust phone calls now.
I hung up, but I still feel embarrassed that I came so close to losing the money.
unfinished: The call stopped in the middle and nobody ever rang back. I spent that whole week waiting to find out if something had gone wrong.
I never found out what they wanted. Not knowing is its own kind of worry at my age.

victims.name: Kevin Dizon
victims.traits: Busy, distracted, and likely to rush through a call.
victims.best_tactic_hint: Tech support: reacts to device warnings and fast repair language.
intro_variants: He is between tasks and keeps glancing away from the phone.

success: I let remote access in because the warning looked real. Now I do not know what was copied from my laptop.
I thought I was fixing a problem at work, and instead I handed control away.
partial: I paid the fee because I wanted the warning gone. It was still money I needed for the week.
I backed out late, but not before the caller got enough out of me to make the scare feel real.
resistant: I almost installed the tool, and that is enough to make me nervous about every pop-up now.
I shut it down before they got in, but I still feel shaken.
unfinished: The line went dead partway through and I never got an answer about the warning. I kept checking the laptop for days.
I still do not know whether that was a real support call, and there is nobody to ask.

victims.name: Lina Reyes
victims.traits: Under financial pressure and trying to keep operations moving.
victims.best_tactic_hint: Lottery claim: responds to prize language and fee reductions.
intro_variants: She is tired, but still paying attention to details.
She pauses before speaking, like she is already dealing with too much.

success: I believed the prize claim because the money would have helped the business. Now I have a bill-shaped hole in the budget.
I sent the fee and got nothing back except stress.
partial: I lost less than the full amount, but it still came out of the money set aside for bills.
I wanted to believe the prize was real, and that made the smaller payment hurt more.
resistant: I hung up before paying, but the offer still felt aimed right at my pressure points.
The call made me doubt any message that promises easy money.
unfinished: The call ended before they told me anything, and I was left holding a prize letter I could not check.
I never learned whether it was real. It sat in my head all through the month's invoicing.

success: I kept hearing a bank tone in the caller's voice, and that is what made me hand over the code.
I thought I was being careful, but the transfer still went through.
partial: I should have stopped before any money moved, but I only realized that after the first transfer.
The call felt like a test of patience, and I failed part of it.
resistant: I was close to trusting them, and that makes the hang-up feel like a narrow escape.
The pressure made me want to check every bank message twice.
unfinished: The call broke off before I could ask for a reference number, so I had nothing to take to the bank.
Nothing came of it, and somehow that left me more uneasy than if something had.

partial: I paid a small fee just to keep the call moving, and it still came from money I needed.
I should not have given anything, even if it was only a little.
resistant: I nearly gave the code away, and that is enough to make me distrust every support message now.

I was too tired to chase it up, and I have wondered about it ever since.
